fine_trace.note: Attacker-controlled bytes (the last third of the persist_fuzzer input, written to the dynamic-resource file) are read from disk into raw_packet; the packet length (4) is also attacker-controlled via the preceding fread of size at line 892.
A PDU is created with size 0, so pdu->alloc_size == 0 and the heap buffer allocated inside coap_pdu_init is only pdu->max_hdr_size bytes.

Root cause: with alloc_size == 0 the allocation is exactly max_hdr_size (6) bytes and pdu->token = buf + pdu->max_hdr_size points one byte past the end of the heap region, so any read of pdu->token[0] is a 1-byte heap-buffer-overflow. The fix (c1147eb096) allocates max(2, pdu->alloc_size) + max_hdr_size.
The 4 attacker-controlled packet bytes are handed to the parser together with the size-0 PDU; session->proto is COAP_PROTO_UDP so the header size is 4 and length == hdr_size.
hdr_size = coap_pdu_parse_header_size(COAP_PROTO_UDP, data) == 4 and length == 4, so resize(pdu, 0) is a no-op: the 6-byte allocation (alloc_size == 0) is kept and pdu->token is not moved.
used_size becomes 0 (4 - 4), so the PDU contains no bytes at/after pdu->token; memcpy at line 1567 only fills the 4 header bytes before pdu->token.
The first header byte 0x4D (version bits 01, TKL nibble 0xD) yields e_token_length == 13 == COAP_TOKEN_EXT_1B_TKL, selecting the extended-token branch that reads pdu->token[0].
Sink: pdu->token[0] is read although pdu->used_size == 0 and pdu->alloc_size == 0; token points one byte past the 6-byte heap allocation, so this READ of size 1 is the reported heap-buffer-overflow.
